facts.value: Imprivata, Inc. (NYSE; Lexington, MA; healthcare IT security)
Thoma Bravo, LLC, through Project Brady Holdings, LLC (Parent) and Project Brady Merger Sub, Inc., affiliates of Thoma Bravo Fund XII, L.P.

$19.25 per share in cash, all cash; funded by an equity commitment from Thoma Bravo Fund XII of up to $548,148,554 plus up to $20,000,000; optional debt financing, no financing condition; total funds about $568.7 million (pp. 58–60)
bidder-led: Thoma Bravo’s approaches and unsolicited 03/09/2016 indication at $15.00 led the Board to hire Barclays and, on 05/05/2016, to canvass other parties

Early 2015 and June 2015: Thoma Bravo informally approached and briefly met the Company, expressing potential interest; no proposal; the Company said it was focused on its business plan. 08/05–10/22/2015: Thoma Bravo-affiliated funds bought 1,213,066 shares (<5%) in the open market for about $17.4 million (p. 26). Not a process: no proposal and no sale effort by the target.
Met (process 1): 7 parties (3 strategic, 4 financial sponsors incl. Thoma Bravo); two debt financing sources that joined Thoma Bravo’s agreement not counted

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices
facts.value: US dollars per share of Imprivata common stock
Barclays Capital Inc. (engaged 04/15/2016); ChipLinnemann, LLC (Chip Linnemann), consultant advising on a sale

Thoma Bravo, which had approached Imprivata informally in 2015 and again in January 2016, sent an unsolicited $15.00 per share cash indication on 03/09/2016. The Board hired Barclays, judged the offer too low and on 05/05/2016 had Barclays canvass 15 parties; seven signed NDAs, and on 06/09/2016 three sponsors bid ($16.50, $17.25 and $17.00–$18.00) while no strategic party bid. The Board advanced the three sponsors and asked for higher bids; Sponsor A would not improve and left, and one more strategic party approached by the new Special Committee declined. Final bid letters went to Sponsor B and Thoma Bravo on 06/24/2016; Sponsor B signalled a much lower value and did not bid by the 07/08 deadline, while Thoma Bravo bid $19.00 with a merger-agreement markup and full equity commitment. Asked for its best and final offer, Thoma Bravo raised to $19.25 on 07/09/2016, and after the Company refused exclusivity the parties signed and announced the all-cash merger on 07/13/2016.

cells.Question: Is this one process with round 0 (Thoma Bravo’s January 2016 approach and 03/09/2016 bid) and rounds opened 05/06 (outreach), 06/12 (three sponsors advanced, improved bids sought) and 06/24/2016 (final bid letters)?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. Most plausible alternative: one “second phase” from 06/12 (the filing’s term), merging rounds 2 and 3 (#26–#31). Lesser: round 1 opened by the 05/05 decision (#6); Strategic 3’s invitation and exit (#27, #29) in round 1.
cells.Why, with page: E6: a selection with a request for improved offers (p. 31) and the first request for final bids (p. 33) each open a round. Gaps of about two months or more without acquirer contact: January 2016 to 03/09/2016 (about 5.5–10 weeks, pp. 26–27); 03/11/2016 to 05/06–05/10/2016 (about 8 weeks, pp. 27–29); June 2015 to January 2016 (about 6–8 months, p. 26).
